headline: Scope approved for buying a front-end loader and pickup truck for airport snow removal.
summary: The two vehicles would replace existing equipment, and the pickup would carry an eight-foot plow. Bids are planned for April, with grant applications due April 30; the worst-case delivery date is May 2028. Separately, the chair may approve a $9,000 change order and a $50,500 supplemental agreement for wildlife fencing, with MassDOT covering the cost. The airport manager, Terry Parker, can now approve commitments alone, and after-hours badge access was tabled.
decisions: Approved authorizing the chair to approve and sign the wildlife fencing supplemental agreement and change order after agency review.
Approved 3-0 the snow removal scope of services, pending revisions and a answer on local vehicle service.
Approved letting the airport manager approve commitments on his own, with abatements still going to the commission.
Tabled after-hours badge access to the administration building until next month's meeting.
discussion: Snow removal vehicles: Members asked about American-made requirements and local vehicle service. The loader would need a waiver, since the waiver process allows 60% US-made components; staff will check local service terms and whether the pre-bid conference should be mandatory.
Main apron closeout: Members asked why the final payment has taken months. The FAA has accepted the closeout, and it needs financial review before the final payment request goes to the FAA.

Runway identifier lights: Members said the lights have failed since they were installed in 2019. The vendor will provide a quote for a new system, and staff will tell the FAA and MassDOT about the problem.
After-hours building access: Members raised liability and slip-and-fall concerns. Staff will check with City Hall on insurance and on a buddy system, and the item returns next month.
